Anya (eng-ml): Heads up — saw a few eval runs where the runner uploaded a trace, S3 returned 200 for parts, but the final manifest never showed up. ~2h later GC removed the partial traces, so the eval shows missing outputs. Anyone seen a GC/upload race? :eyes:
Michael T: ugh. Do you have the root trace id or one sample id? could be the multipart commit failing before manifest write. logs?
Anya (eng-ml): sample_id=eval-2026-03-19-tty-43f2, runner logs: `uploader: parts uploaded, commit manifest -> 409 conflict`, then nothing. I dug and saw the GC job processed that bucket 5m later and deleted `trace-prefix/eval-2026-03-19-tty-43f2/parts/` because manifest missing.
Samir K: repro'd locally. If the manifest write returns 409 (object exists) we treat it as success, but in our case 409 came from a transient S3 condition and the uploader aborted without recording manifest pointer in the DB. GC only looks at DB pointers -> deletes orphaned parts.
Samir K: quick repro script I used:
```bash
# simulate multipart then fail manifest commit
python tests/repro_multipart_race.py --trace eval-rr
# produces missing-manifest.tar.gz with parts present but no DB pointer
```
Anya (eng-ml): OK that matches. So we need uploader idempotency + GC to check S3 markers before pruning.
Olivia R: two approaches: 1) leave current GC but add a short grace window + check for an `upload_in_progress` marker object (zero-byte) before deleting; 2) add a lease/lock in Redis at upload start; GC skips leased prefixes. Option 1 is lower friction.
Michael T: agree on marker. Implementation: uploader writes `trace-prefix/<id>/_UPLOADING` before parts, then atomically rename/put manifest. GC will check for `_UPLOADING` key and skip if present. If manifest appears, uploader removes `_UPLOADING`.
Samir K: edge: uploader crash after parts uploaded but before manifest — marker stays forever. GC will never remove unless we add TTL on marker. Suggest marker has metadata `expires_at` or we use object lifecycle rule + GC also purges stale markers older than X.
Anya (eng-ml): good call. TTL of 6 hours for marker? current retention for incomplete artifacts is 48h but we don't want markers to block forever. Maybe marker TTL = 12h and GC deletes parts if marker older than TTL.
Michael T: also add DB reconciliation job: list S3 prefixes, compare DB pointers, and emit alert for orphaned parts older than 1h. That will catch weird states and create tickets.
Olivia R: I'll sketch a small change: `uploader.go` pseudo:```go
// before multipart
putObject("<prefix>/_UPLOADING", "{\"expires\": 168}")
// upload parts...
commitManifest()
deleteObject("<prefix>/_UPLOADING")
```
and GC currently: `if manifest_missing && !uploading_marker { delete_parts() }` -> change to `if manifest_missing && (!uploading_marker || marker_stale) { delete_parts() }`.
trace-uploader-bot: [info] uploader-1234 started multipart upload for eval-2026-03-19-tty-43f2
Samir K: I'll open a small PR to add marker write+delete + marker TTL check in GC. Also add unit test that simulates `commitManifest` throwing `409` and ensures GC doesn't delete within TTL. PR will include a tiny integ test that runs in CI with a mocked S3.
CI Bot: Heads up — please add the integ test to `eng-ml` CI matrix; we can gate with `s3-mock` label.
Anya (eng-ml): Thanks — Samir can you also add an alerting rule for "orphaned-parts > 1h"? want a pager if it spikes.
Samir K: yep. will add alert + PR (#3412) with code + test + a runbook snippet explaining manual cleanup: `aws s3 rm --recursive s3://eval-traces/<prefix>`
Michael T: one more: instrument uploader metrics: `uploader.manifests_failed` with tags `reason=409|timeout`. will help pinpoint frequency.
Olivia R: put a comment in the runbook about eventual migration: once we roll this out, run the reconciliation job to find existing orphaned prefixes and reingest or delete as appropriate.
Anya (eng-ml): cool. Thanks all. plan: Samir PR by EOD, I’ll schedule GC change for the week after once tests pass. :thumbsup:
